title: ::: K-IG 교육 영어듣기훈련프로그램 | 기초2 | 제 001 회 강의 :::
label: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 008 ]

blocks.text: It takes the Earth about 365 and a quarter days to travel once around the Sun. A calendar year, however, has only 365 days, so the calendar and the seasons slowly drift apart. To fix this, an extra day, February 29, is added every four years. These years are called leap years. But adding a day every four years is slightly too much, because the real difference is a little less than six hours a year. So years that end in 00 are leap years only if they can be divided by 400. That is why 2000 was a leap year, but 1900 was not.
